thread:
olivia: SE flagged a POC with BetaLogix where their integration suddenly started returning 401s after they clicked "reissue key" in our console. Can someone from eng presales triage?

dan: pinging raj/ops. Do we have the raw API response or client logs?

raj: I pulled the initial API response they sent: ```json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid for project: poc-beta-77"}
```

olivia: They used curl: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-beta-ttl" \  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "input":"test"}'
```

ops-bot: [audit] key-lookup id=lk_33b1, key=sk-poc-beta-ttl, status=DELETED, checked_at=2026-03-21T09:12:47Z

raj: ops logs show the key was deleted and a replacement sk-poc-beta-new was created during their reissue action. If they kept the old token in their app it will 401.

dan: Could the UI have performed a rotate-in-place and invalidated the token immediately? SE says the customer didn't change anything on their side.

olivia: SE mentioned they clicked reissue then refreshed the POC project page. They reported the new key string in the console but the client still used the old one.

sam: Two quick mitigations: 1) ask them to copy/paste the new key and retry; 2) if urgent, we can generate an emergency-scoped key for 15 minutes while they update. Security prefers no re-enables.

raj: Also confirm they're not hitting embeddings/admin endpoints with a generate-only key. That would cause 403 rather than 401 but worth checking.

dan: Let's give the SE a concise troubleshooting checklist they can send to the customer.

olivia: Draft checklist: 1) paste exact key string the client is sending (no truncation), 2) try curl with new key sk-poc-beta-new and paste response, 3) include any x-rw-trace header values from the response, 4) confirm which endpoint (region) they're calling, 5) confirm token scope if using different API features, 6) if still failing, request emergency key from eng with justification.

ops-bot: [trace] request id=req_7c5, trace=x-rw-trace-7c5, path=/v1/generate, key=sk-poc-beta-new, result=OK, latency_ms=112

sam: I'll prepare a short support play that SE can paste: ```
- Confirm you're using the new key shown in the console (sk-poc-beta-new).
- Run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"ping"}'
- If 401, include the full response and any x-rw-trace header.
- If 403, check token scopes and switch to a key with required scopes.
- For emergency access request: reply here with the reason and we'll issue a short TTL key.
```

dan: Also note for the SE: reissue action intentionally deletes old key to avoid orphaned credentials. We'll add UI copy to warn about immediate invalidation.

olivia: Good idea. Can eng product own that small UI tweak? It'll reduce POC friction.

raj: I'll also add a small test to the POC onboarding checklist: after key creation, call /v1/health and /v1/generate from the SE machine to verify the key works across endpoints.

olivia: Perfect. I'll send the play to the SE, offer the emergency key option, and loop back to the customer. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: leaving a note for record: prefer issuing emergency keys as time-limited and scope-restricted; log issuance in audit.

olivia: closing swarm, will update the CRM deal with the resolution and next steps.
